about.text: Pure milk fat, with at least 99.8 % fat and next to no water or milk solids, made by separating melted butter or cream and drying the oil under vacuum. Traded in drums as an industrial ingredient for chocolate, ice cream and recombined milk.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: 35–40 % cream concentrated to about 75 % fat at about 60 °C, homogenised to invert the phases, separated to about 99.5 % fat oil
Smoke point 182 °C; melts at 30–32 °C and sets at 18–20 °C (Norwegian smørolje, 99.9% fat)
Estonian võiõli is the base for reconstituted butter; in New Zealand Fonterra's NZMP sells AMF as an ingredient
